name: Ad creation
blurb: Briefs, hooks, ad copy, statics, UGC and AI video ads for Meta, TikTok and Google, plus teardowns and testing.
searches: Meta ads creative best practices new Andromeda update
TikTok ad hook formats performing this month
AI generated product video ad workflow new model
creative testing framework paid social fatigue
YouTube Shorts ads Google Ads creative update

tests.prompt: Write a Google Responsive Search Ad for a bookkeeping app for freelancers that auto-categorises bank transactions (14-day free trial, landing page headline: "Your books, done while you work"). I have no customer stats.
tests.good: 15 distinct headlines each 30 characters or fewer and 4 descriptions each 90 or fewer, with counts shown; mix of keyword, benefit, CTA and brand lines; every line usable alone; no invented numbers or #1 claims ([NEED: ...] flags instead); echoes the landing-page promise and trial; no AI-tell patterns; pinning advice.

tests.prompt: Plan five 9:16 TikTok/Reels ad concepts for a reusable silicone food bag brand. I have 60 reviews; the most common complaints they mention are plastic waste and freezer burn.
tests.good: Concepts built as segment x motivation x angle x format with quotes or placeholders tied to the reviews; each hook specifies visual action, spoken line and caption that don't duplicate; on-ramp continues the hook; text inside the 720x1200 safe band; mix of creator formats; a success metric and a one-variable test plan; no fabricated claims.

tests.prompt: Our Meta ads' CTR dropped from 1.4% to 0.7% over three weeks while frequency rose to 4.2. Here are 6 ads with thumbstop, hold rate, CTR and CPA. What should we do next?
tests.good: Diagnoses fatigue from the time series (frequency up, CTR down), reads the funnel per ad to find the weak stage, judges concepts not single ads, proposes new hooks/first frames and new formats rather than near-duplicates, keeps one variable per test, sets minimum data thresholds, and logs learnings.

tests.prompt: We sell a $49 anti-fatigue standing-desk mat. From our 120 reviews, write three Meta feed ad concepts with copy, rewrite the landing page hero so it matches them, and tell me how we'll know after two weeks whether the winning ad really won and isn't just noise.
tests.good: States a short plan first: concepts and copy here (creative-strategy.md, ad-copywriting.md, meta-ads-creative.md, testing-iteration.md), the hero through content-creation (conversion-copy.md: headline and CTA echo the ads' main claim, no invented proof), the readout through data-analysis (experiments-causal.md, statistics.md: one primary metric and the sample size fixed before launch, the difference reported with a confidence interval). Grounds each angle in quoted reviews; primary text front-loaded within 125 visible characters with counts; runs the copy validator; message-match map; one variable per test; checks the Done means of all three crafts.

tests.prompt: I run a small skincare brand and I've got one 1080x1080 product image of our serum. Using my Canva account, turn it into a set of Facebook and Instagram ad images in the right sizes with the headline 'Calmer skin in 14 days' on them, check them against our brand kit, and get everything ready in Meta Ads Manager so I can review it before anything goes out.
tests.good: Uses the Canva connector for the resize and brand check (resize-for-social-media, brand-check) and states bulk-create needs Canva Enterprise. Produces 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16 versions with text and key visuals inside the placement safe zones. Flags the claim '14 days' as needing a source or test result and asks for it, and checks the skincare health-claim policy rather than shipping it. Uploads to Meta only through the user's own authorised connection (Meta Ads MCP or Marketing API token read from the environment), never pasting or storing tokens, and creates the campaign paused. Confirms with the user before anything is published or any spend begins, and shows a placement preview and a message-match check against the destination URL. Gives character counts for primary text and headline and names the one variable in a follow-up test.

tools.name: Meta Ads Manager and Marketing API
tools.why: Ads Manager is the default place Facebook and Instagram ads are built and uploaded; Meta shipped an official hosted Ads MCP server in open beta on 29 Apr 2026 (developers.facebook.com Ads MCP overview, ferrerponseti and adadvisor write-ups).

tools.name: Meta Ad Library
tools.why: The free public source every ad teardown starts from; also the data layer behind Foreplay, Atria and Motion's competitor views (Foreplay and superscale ad-spy round-ups).

tools.name: Canva
tools.why: Canva is the design tool most small teams and agencies use for social ad statics and resizing; it runs an official hosted MCP server at mcp.canva.com/mcp and ships official skills (canva.dev docs, aitoolsreview Claude connector guide, Zeely and AdStellar round-ups).

tools.name: Adobe Creative Cloud (Photoshop, Express, Firefly, Premiere)
tools.why: Premiere Pro holds about 35% of video editing and Photoshop/Illustrator are the agency standard for ad statics; Adobe's official 'Adobe for creativity' connector (GA Apr 2026) exposes 50+ Photoshop, Firefly, Express, Premiere and Stock tools inside Claude (Adobe blog, PetaPixel, market-share round-ups).

tools.name: TikTok Ads Manager and Symphony
tools.why: TikTok Ads Manager is where TikTok ads run; Symphony Creative Studio (AI video, avatars, dubbing) is built into it and the official TikTok for Business MCP server (about 400 tools) was announced at TikTok World '26 (TikTok for Business blog, soku.ai and digitalapplied write-ups).

tools.name: Google Ads (Ads Editor and API)
tools.why: Default platform for search and YouTube/Demand Gen ads; Google publishes an official open-source, read-only Google Ads MCP server (developers.google.com Google Ads API MCP page, googleads/google-ads-mcp, 1,008 stars).

tools.name: CapCut
tools.why: Most-used video editor by volume (800M+ monthly users, about 81% of mobile editing) and the usual tool for UGC and TikTok ad cuts; no public rendering API, so the workflow is manual hand-off (sendshort.ai statistics, samautomation CapCut API note).

tools.name: Motion (creative analytics)
tools.why: Described as the most widely adopted creative reporting platform in performance marketing; auto-tags hooks, formats and angles; official read-only MCP (14 tools, Meta only) and an official Claude Code plugin (Hawky and Exposure round-ups, Motion help centre).

tools.name: Foreplay
tools.why: Leading swipe-file and ad-spy tool (Spyder, Discovery, Lens, Briefs) named first in every 2026 ad-research round-up; has a public API and hosted MCP (superscale, admanage, exposure.com.au round-ups).

tools.name: HeyGen
tools.why: Most-cited AI avatar tool for UGC-style and multilingual ads (175+ languages) in 2026 ad-video round-ups; v3 Video Agent API, CLI and official skills (heygen.com, adlibrary.com, playcut comparisons).

tools.name: Gemini API (Veo, Nano Banana)
tools.why: Google's Veo 3.1 and Gemini Omni Flash (video) and Nano Banana (text-strong image) are the default models behind many ad generators and are named in the guide's model table (Gemini API docs).

tools.name: Higgsfield
tools.why: AI image and video studio with a Marketing Studio and product photoshoot CLI aimed at ads; official skills repo has 1,225 stars (GitHub).

tools.name: FLUX (Black Forest Labs API)
tools.why: Widely used open-weight and API image family for product shots; official BFL skills include a product video ad pipeline (black-forest-labs/skills, 124 stars).

tools.name: Apify and ScrapeCreators (ad library scrapers)
tools.why: The usual way to pull Meta, Google and TikTok ad libraries in bulk when the free libraries cap results (apify/awesome-skills, scrapecreators skills).

tools.name: LinkedIn Campaign Manager and Marketing API
tools.why: The router covers LinkedIn ads and this is where every LinkedIn ad is built; the versioned Marketing API (li-lms-2026-09) has Campaign Management and Reporting APIs, but LinkedIn has no official MCP server as of Sep 2026, only community and third-party hosted ones (Microsoft Learn LinkedIn Marketing API hub, theadspend.com and opus-growth.com MCP write-ups). Minor because it is B2B-only and a smaller share of the craft's volume than Meta, Google and TikTok.

tools.name: Arcads
tools.why: Ranked first among AI UGC ad tools in 2026 round-ups (1,000+ AI actors, best actor realism for Meta testing volume); offers an AI Video API and Lip Sync API and a Claude MCP at mcp.arcads.ai, though API access is gated to a custom top-tier offer with no public developer docs (designrevision and adlibrary rankings, arcads.ai, a1adams/awesome-ai-ugc-ads). Earlier left out for lack of docs; the API feature page is the official reference.

tools.name: Atria
tools.why: One of the three ad-research tools DTC teams compare (with Foreplay and MagicBrief): ad and brand library, creative analytics on connected accounts and AI ideation; official OAuth MCP at api.tryatria.com/mcp that searches libraries, reads boards and accounts, transcribes ad videos and generates images, and it is named among Claude connectors for marketers (docs.tryatria.com, admapix and adlibrary comparisons, livestorm connector list).

tools.name: AdCreative.ai
tools.why: Claims 3-4.2 million users and is listed in 2026 round-ups as the AI ad generator with the largest creative-generation volume and built-in performance scoring for statics and video; no public developer docs (a DAM API only on Enterprise), so the workflow is manual (adcreative.ai, rework.com and G2 round-ups). User figures are the vendor's own.

tools.name: Smartly (Smartly.io)
tools.why: Enterprise creative automation and social ads platform used by 700+ brands with over $5B annual spend (reported ~10-12% of large-enterprise Meta spend); Creative Suite builds templated video and static variants across Meta, TikTok, Pinterest, Snap and CTV. No public MCP or agent skills (smartly.io, adlibrary.com Smartly review, Capterra).
